name: solve_reachable_pose_sequence
summary: Select an arm-effector pair and solve chained IK for an entire task-defined TCP-pose sequence.

generality.rationale: Consumes generic ordered TCP poses and physical arm-effector pairs without knowing whether the task is grasping, placing, pressing, or another motion primitive.
assumptions: Discrete chained IK across task-complete waypoints is a useful feasibility test.
limitations: No continuous collision checking, dynamics, force control, motion execution, or task-effect verification.
tested_tasks: robotwin/press-stapler-aloha-agilex (selection behavior extracted from harness_v2 multi-arm planner)

level.rationale: Ranks physical candidates, transforms TCP poses through profiles and frames, and solves every ordered stage with chained seeds.

provenance.failure_gap: Arm selection and whole-sequence reachability were trapped inside a linear-contact-specific wrapper and could not be reused by grasp or place tasks.
evidence: Qwen fixed on right_arm and brute-forced raw IK in iter_001 even though a left-arm complete sequence was available.
